text:
What are you talking about? The 30-series is supposedly good for it's price. The only issue is the tarriffs, silicon/copper shortage, and miners all coming together in one huge coincidence, that Nvidia wouldn't have control over. 3060 ti and 3080 existed at a good value, if prices weren't inflated af a lot of mid builders would buy the 3060ti and budget high-end with the 3080. Thing is, the 3060Ti at $400 is only a sub $70 away from when the 970 launched and $20 when the 1070 launched, both cards who were nearly equivalent to their respective previous generation's flagship. The 3060ti is on that same boat, literally a few percent away from a freaking 2080Ti and a 3070. 

And the 3080? Literally is what the 1080ti was like prior, $700 msrp and a monstrous card that's near Titan levels of its generation. 10% at best away from the 3090, a "consumer Titan". 3080Ti only existed as a way for Nvidia to shave off profit loss because the 3080 was actually making Nvidia lose revenue. YES, the 3080 was so freaking good for it's value they had to slow down production of it since 3080s are basically lower binned GA102s and the cost to sell is practically halved from their best binned ones for the 3090. They had to cut back losses by making them instead 3080tis and sell them at a higher price. That's why Nvidia's refreshing their lineup again with Super cards to compensate with 3080 loss and discontinuing the 3080. What could've prevented this was AMD actually having more stock of the 6900xt and revealing it later so Nvidia would be scared the same way they were against Vega 64 prior to launch that they priced the 1080Ti at $700 because they didn't know if it was better or equivalent at a better price.

And I am a person who went from 1080Ti to 3080, all for the literal same price I spent on my 1080Ti Strix back then for $800 to a 3080 FTW3 for $810. Don't tell that's not good card because it is for it's price, which is nearly double the 2080's/1080Ti's performance.

text:
If you don't try to make use of any of the additional physical cores on the 3000 series; sure, pretty similar. Try ticking that RT option in graphics and see what happens to the 1080 who only has software support, vs the 3060's physical RT cores on the GPU. Not to mention 3000 series cards perform less efficiently at lower resolutions. So the 1080 can keep up with the 3060 with every new feature of the past 5 years turned off, sure. Very equal. 

Only benchmarks that matter these days compare several resolutions, along with RT, DLSS, and FSR turned on and off. Cherry picking resolutions and graphic settings doesn't give much useful information for actual performance. In the past, sure, slap two cards against each and there weren't specific features or different physically built cores onto the gpu to compare. Now Nvidia and AMD each have their own bevy of different physical cores, leading to very different performances depending on the actual settings. Just comparing fps at different resolutions with nothing else is misleading at best.

My gigabyte aorus extreme 1080 ti was dying even attempting to do what a 3060 is actually capable of because RT cores weren't built onto GPUs until the 2000 series, yet this video suggests the 1080, a step below my 1080 ti, would be the same, if not better, than a 3060. That's just not true.

text: @weskerkings651  I would advice against anything 4 core in 2021 - especially since we are about to be in 2022.. author: @mrbrad4637
@weskerkings651

text: @weskerkings651  I've not seen too many benchmarks if any on an 85w 3060 (that is the Max Q version) .. my laptop has the fastest 130w 3060 Max P and the performance is phenomenal - I can max out every current AAA game and get 85 to 120+ fps in all of them bar ms flight Sim which runs around 75fps in cockpit view where I fly.. even Battlefield 2042 which recommends a desktop 3060 I get incredible performance.. Just because RDR2 gets 60fps on the 85w 3060 doesn't mean others will due to the 4 core CPU as RDR2 is a game from 2019 - many current games are becoming bottlenecked by 4 core CPUs therefore a minimum of 6 cores is recommended in my opinion... Put it this way my Ryzen 7 3750H with a 90w 2060 struggled to maintain even 45fps on warzone with everything set to low yet on my new laptop with 8 cores and a 130w 3060 I can max warzone out with even ray tracing on and DLSS off!! And I get 90 to 122fps.. Personally I think an 85w 3060 would still be a decent performaner if paired with a 6 core CPU but I think if you get it paired with a 4 core you'll be very unhappy with upcoming games... Search YouTube for benchmarks on games you plan to play with  the model laptop you're thinking of getting and you'll find numerous videos I'm sure as that's how I decided on my Dell G15 as it's performance in benchmarks was incredible.. honestly I don't think you'll find much of a price difference between the one you're thinking of getting compared to a 6 or 8 core CPU and a 130w version of the 3060.. here in Australia there is probably around only $300-$400 AUD difference in price between a 4core CPU with an 85w 3060 compared to an 8core CPU with the 130w 3060 yet for spending that extra few hundred you'll be getting up to double the FPS depending on if the game can use more than 4 cores and you'll also be future proof
